_doc: AUTHORED, and deliberately small. It carries the newspaper corpus's LOT-AND-BLOCK addresses — a printed statement of the form 'lot N, in block M' — and nothing else. There is one today. Nothing here authors geometry or names a structure: the block number resolves through data/traces/thompson_block_numbering.json, the lot number through the numbering scheme committed there, and WHICH committed roof stands at the resolved address is derived by tools/lot_addresses.py from the lot polygon in data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json. The policy is docs/LOT-ADDRESS.md and the liberty is L216.
why_this_file_exists: T-0358 committed the Thompson plat's block numbering so that the corpus's one lot-and-block address could resolve to ground. It resolved to a POLYGON and stopped there: the roof standing on that polygon went on carding as an anonymous count-unit, so the most precisely placed building in the whole corpus was, to a visitor walking Lake Street, a vacant one-room frame cottage. This file is the address; tools/lot_addresses.py is what spends it.

addresses.address_text: LOT No. 7, in block No. 16, one lot east of Haddock's Tavern, on Lake street, in the town of Chicago
addresses.title: The dwelling-house on lot 7, block 16

stood_on_the_lot.note: The notice says 'There is on said lot a large Dwelling-House'. Four of the six printings carry the words unbroken. WHAT IS DRAWN AT THIS ADDRESS IS NOT THIS HOUSE: the roof standing on the lot is the 665-roof programme's own count-unit, dealt to the D3 family before this address resolved to anything, and its footprint is a 5.36 x 6.38 m one-room cottage. The source says LARGE and the fabric under the address does not answer to that word. The address is what this record gains; the fabric is unchanged and still conjectural, and the mismatch is stated rather than repaired by re-dealing the block's family mix — which is a second demonstration and is filed as its own ticket.

NOT DRAWN, and this is the reason. The notice's second structure is a well, and it is documented as plainly as the house. The town has no well: there is no well archetype in generators/archetypes, no well appears in any committed structure or yard record, and drawing the first one would be raising a new kind of object for the whole scene rather than placing a known one. Inventing a shaft, a curb and a sweep for this lot alone would put conjectural geometry beside a documented word and would be the only well in Chicago. It is filed as its own ticket instead, and the address says here that the well is documented and absent.

advertiser.note: The notice ends 'For terms enquire of G. SPRING' and says NOTHING ELSE about him. He is the man to apply to, which is not a statement that he owned the lot, and is certainly not a statement that he lived in the house — the same G. Spring is the attorney whose office the papers put second door west of the corner of Franklin and South Water. So this house is not named for him, and the register's business_g_spring is not moved here. T-0412 is the same trap read from the other side: a building offered FOR SALE must not mint a placement on its vendor.

printings_not_cited.why: The transcription interleaves two columns and the column edge removed the tavern's name — the reading itself records that the letters before "k'n Tavern" are gone and that the house is 'a large [?]ase'. The lot and the block survive in it, so it corroborates; it is not cited as a legible printing of the address.

The same notice with the neighbouring tavern printed 'Maddock's' and the street 'Lako' — an optical corruption of a name this project holds under another reading. It corroborates the lot, the block and the well; it is not cited as a legible printing.

addresses.confidence_note: THE ADDRESS IS READ; WHERE THE ADDRESS LANDS IS THE BOTTOM TIER, and the chain is short enough to state in one breath. The words 'lot 7, block 16' are a direct reading of four printings. The block number is `inferred` — three blocks counted east of the one numeral the Wright sheet shows (data/traces/thompson_block_numbering.json). The lot number is `conjectural` twice over: four lots to a block face is a reading of one block, the lot lines it numbers are the plat module's and are drawn from no sheet, and the counter-clockwise scheme itself was read off block 18. A chain is as strong as its weakest link, so which committed roof stands at this address is graded at the bottom tier — the same grade the roof already carried, and it does not rise because a documented address was put on it.
